title: Trajectory heatmap and buyers' payoff recon
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: A compact research ticket to produce a competitor trajectory heatmap (model capability x time) cross-referenced with buyer payoff curves (latency, price, and integration friction). The goal is a prioritized list of model migration risks for Redwood customers and actionable probes for PM and Field teams. Deliverables: 1) heatmap artifact (SVG + CSV), 2) scoring rubric, 3) shortlist of 6 competitor behaviors to monitor, 4) four field interview guides, 5) recommendations for fallback bundling and two product experiments.
acceptance_criteria: Heatmap artifact with source data and reproducible notebook published to Drive
Scoring rubric (0-10) for migration risk with examples
Top-6 competitor behavior signals instrumented in model-scouting pipeline
At least four buyer interviews scheduled and two completed with notes
Concrete recommendations for two product experiments (rollout and bundling)
updates: 2026-02-10 Aisha Rahman Created ticket and seeded initial list of competitors (OpenLlama variants, Falcon family, Mistral-Chat, Claude-lite forks).
2026-02-17 Luca Moreno scoped data inputs: public model release cadence, cloud provider latency reports, and anonymized customer query samples from Console telemetry. Linked dataset ingestion PR.
2026-02-22 Research spike: synthetic buyer payoff curves created from 120k request traces. Observed two clusters: latency-sensitive search workloads and cost-sensitive batch embedding workloads.

2026-02-28 Engineering review: ENG-42318 (ingest-workload-normalizer) added as dependency to normalize token counts across providers. Risk: competitor latency numbers often measured under different sequence lengths; applied normalization offsets.
2026-03-03 Design feedback: DES-902 recommended a condensed heatmap color palette for accessibility and an interactive filter for region and model family.
2026-03-05 Field ops: scheduled buyer interviews with three mid-market customers for 2026-03-09 and 2026-03-11. Interview guide v0.2 uploaded.
notes: Trade-off: using public release dates yields coarse-grained trajectory; supplementing with GitHub commit activity increases noise but improves lead indicators.
Decision so far: use normalized P50 latency where available, fallback to reported median when not.
Potential blind spot: private enterprise fine-tuned variants that are not public; will capture via customer interviews and field reports.
